title: About WoWSP
subtitle: World of WarShip Panel
description: A desktop dashboard for World of Warships: standalone replay review with a holographic 3D map, plus an in-game transparent overlay for live stats lookup.
trivia01: Yukikaze's torpedoes reach just 8 km, yet each carries 21,367 alpha at 76 knots — the same Type F3 hardware as Shimakaze's, on a much faster reload.
trivia02: Mash the M key twice: during the tactical-map camera transition the view briefly lifts high enough to aim at enemies hiding behind islands.
trivia03: Near the end of Operation Raptor Rescue, a little paper-folded ship sometimes drifts outside the map border: shells cannot touch it, only ship-launched torpedoes can — and a hit unlocks the hidden 「Insert Coin」 achievement.
trivia04: Yamato's 460 mm guns play the overmatch rule: any armor thinner than 1/14.3 of the caliber (about 32 mm) is penetrated outright, no matter how steep the angle — if it overmatches, it penetrates. A failed penetration usually means the shell never hit an overmatchable plate in the first place — for example, the armor on the bow, stern or deck that exceeds the threshold — not that overmatch failed.
trivia05: Radar spots ships straight through islands and smoke, and hydroacoustic search does the same when hunting surface ships. Do not lump 「hydro」 and 「submarine surveillance」 together: submarine detection is limited by depth, not islands — down to a mere 2 km at maximum depth. WG and Lesta currently share the same rules; the island-blocking concept Lesta once announced has yet to ship.
trivia06: The hardest-hitting torpedo in the game does not belong to a destroyer but to British battleships: the 622 mm Mk I at 29,367 alpha, carried by Rodney, Duncan and St. Vincent.
trivia07: Kitakami and her 40 torpedo tubes were once judged too toxic for the game: pulled in 2015, she only returned eight years later (December 2023) as a Tier X cruiser.
trivia08: Shimakaze's 20 km torpedoes are nicknamed the 「wall of skill」: 62 knots slow and spotted from 2.5 km, dodgeable by anyone — the name is pure sarcasm.
trivia09: Magazine detonations haunted players for over nine years until they were removed outright in late November 2024 (Update 13.11), retiring the legendary Juliet Charlie 「no-detonation」 flag along the way.
trivia10: Shell damage math: over-pens pay 10%, penetrations 33%, citadel hits 100% — and destroyers have no citadel at all, so AP of 280 mm or larger is capped at 10% against them.
trivia11: Operation Killer Whale can spawn a friendly bot Benson commanded by Commander Jenkins: keep him alive until victory and you earn the one-time hidden 「Save Commander Jenkins」 achievement.
trivia12: The largest guns on the WG server belong to Satsuma: four twin 510 mm mounts on a 35-second reload, based on the real IJN「Super Yamato」design study. On the Lesta server, the 533 mm guns went to the German super-battleship Schwaben instead.
trivia13: Actually, it is this pig talking to you right now. Probably. Hmph hmph.
trivia14: Wowo-nyan (窝窝娘), the official VTuber of the Chinese server, is actually based on a catshark — not on the Schlieffen. Hmph hmph.
trivia15: These fun facts were hand-picked by the pig itself, which refuses to take any responsibility for their accuracy. Hmph hmph.
trivia16: Different shell types on the same gun can have different maximum ranges: Yamato's AP falls short of her HE — shell weight and ballistics differ, so not every shell actually flies out to the theoretical maximum range.
trivia17: In Operations and event modes, hydroacoustic search can even「hear」coastal bunkers — the pig thinks this looks more like a bug than a design choice.
trivia18: Black's torpedoes hit for a hefty 21,600 a pop and stay hidden until a mere 0.9 km out — at 43 knots they crawl, but every hit bites.
trivia20: Edinburgh's in-game model really does hide gold: she went down carrying Soviet gold in 1942, and the model keeps the Easter egg.
trivia22: Quackaducko stows her mines inside the X turret position at the stern; incidentally, mines are currently a Lesta-server-only weapon.
trivia23: Valparaíso carries six Repair Parties out of the box — seven once you pick the Superintendent skill — a floating hospital, and then some.
trivia24: The WG server briefly had Vyazma and Oregon: burst fire from a limited stock of special shells, plus excellent penetration, made them a force in Ranked for a while; but WG knew full well they were too unbalanced and never intended them to stay.
trivia25: WG once released a video promising submarines would never be added — well, you know how that turned out.
trivia26: The first radar destroyer was the Pan-Asian Yueyang, released in 2017 — radar is still an optional consumable for her. Grozovoi's radar, meanwhile, never left the 2018 test-concept stage: it was swapped for a Repair Party before she even shipped.
trivia27: Jets have been in World of Warships for ages, yet not one of the old jet aircraft has ever been sent back for a model rework.
trivia28: Aircraft carriers used to exist at odd tiers: the early CV line spanned tiers 4 to 10, with carriers at 5, 7 and 9 before the rework standardized them on even tiers.
trivia29: Japanese heavy cruisers carry their thickest deck armor at low tiers: Furutaka and Aoba boast a 48 mm deck, while from Tier VII onward it shrinks to a mere 27–32 mm.
trivia30: The French heavy cruiser line launched with an unusually deep consumable loadout, and back then restocking premium consumables cost credits every battle (the practice survived until Update 0.9.4 in 2020) — earning the line a reputation as a credit incinerator.
trivia31: The original Buffalo had torpedoes — today she is guns only.
trivia32: Weser was converted from the Hipper-class hull of Seydlitz — and among her Hipper-blooded cousins, the lowest-tier one has the best concealment: just 11.7 km by sea, beating Admiral Hipper, Roon and Prinz Eugen.
trivia33: Myōkō has more clones than any other silver ship — reskins, premium editions and event versions together could man a whole fleet.
trivia34: WG produced a full How it Works video series; if you have fewer than 1,000 battles, go watch them — that is your homework.
trivia35: Weser's Arado Ar 197 biplane is the fastest biplane in the game — 172 knots flat out, outrunning even Midway's torpedo bombers.
trivia36: Remember to upgrade Clemson's hull: her main guns turn from single mounts into twins, doubling her firepower.
trivia38: WoWSP was almost entirely written by Chinese large language models, mainly the DeepSeek and GLM series. Hmph hmph.
trivia39: Fusō's HE takes a good 18 seconds to come down at her natural maximum range — a glorious rainbow of a trajectory. Still, Yamato and Satsuma, lobbing shells out past 26 km, keep theirs in the air even longer.
trivia40: World of Warships was originally developed by the Lesta studio and run by WG; after the Russia-Ukraine war split Belarus-based WG and Russia-based Lesta, Lesta took over the Russian business and now develops and runs its own standalone server, World of Ships (Мир кораблей), while WG keeps the international game.
trivia41: In the Soviet battleship line, only Tier IV Gangut was genuinely completed and commissioned; Tier VI Izmail and Tier IX Sovetsky Soyuz were both laid down but never finished, so they barely count. Off the line, the Tier VI premium Novorossiysk is historical too — she was the Italian Giulio Cesare, handed over to the USSR as war reparations. The rest are all paper designs.
trivia42: During World War II the US launched dozens of Essex-class carriers at dumpling-making speed — in China the class is nicknamed「Dumpling-class」.
trivia43: In one battle, @BestNaomi was sailing Vermont when an enemy Ohio one-salvoed him for 83,079 damage — since then, 「83079」 has become an inside joke among Chinese World of Warships players.
trivia44: Some ships have their own unique horn sounds — press N in port or in battle to sound the horn.
trivia45: Back in 2015–2016, under the old three-hull system, upgrading Mutsuki to her final hull meant trading two 120 mm turrets away for stronger torpedoes — the exact opposite of Clemson's upgrade. The current game no longer does this.
trivia46: At launch, Furutaka's stock hull carried six single 200 mm guns on lethargic turrets and was widely considered a poor configuration; the first upgrade swapped them for single 203 mm Type 3 guns (the same family used from Furutaka through Ibuki), and only the final hull turned the battery into three twin 203 mm turrets.
trivia47: WoWSP actually stands for World of WarShip Pig. Hmph hmph.
trivia48: These little notes were actually written not by the pig, but by the big fat fish DeepSeek. Hmph hmph.
